description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on its own carrier (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER) hung from the oak top, its pad rows on HDR-MATRIX
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used. MOUNTED ON ITS OWN CARRIER BOARD (owner, 2026-10-03, option (c); ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-03): two 1x10 headers (HDR-MATRIX) join its pad rows to the carrier (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER), which hangs from the oak top on three spacers (MECH-MX-*), and CBL-MCU-RIBBON runs from the carrier's J-MCU-C to J-MCU. ONLY ITS PAD ROWS ARE WIRED: it is programmed and recovered over its own USB-C, with its BOOT and RESET buttons (owner, 2026-10-03: 'Program over USB only'), and its pad-row 5V and GND carry its supply, so no back-side pad (TP2, TP3, EN, IO0) is wired. Its USB-C is the instrument's USB port, by the panel-mount extension to the tail face (mechanical/DESIGN.md); NO ESD ARRAY on that path, by the owner's decision (ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-02): the Matrix's own D+/D- reach the ESP32-S3 with nothing between [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf, USB block]. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 4-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED drive and the LED row, the regulator, service header
package: long and narrow, sized in mechanical/drc.echo (main board), 1.6mm (config/body.yaml switch.pcb_t)
notes: ONE board at the thumb level, mouth cap to the end of the right hand (ADR 0017). A TONGUE runs on from its tail end to the etherCON's adapter and carries J-UMB, soldered into both (ADR 0021). The thumb switches solder into it; the key boards connect to it by 12-conductor IDC ribbons (CBL-CHAIN), a through-hole right-angle J-CHAIN header for each in its far band beside the LED row. Parts face up - mechanical/drc.echo gives the room under the key boards and elsewhere. A clearance hole for each U-bolt leg, no edge notches, and a plated PWR_GND hole at each mount, every one on the cassette's bottom plate: the stud, the spacer, the board, then a column's standoff or an end mount's nut (ADR 0022, ADR 0025). Its underside faces the grounded bottom plate over its whole length, so an underside part needs a window cut in the plate (hardware/boards/main-board/README.md). 1.6mm, as the key boards, its top pressed against the thumb switches' housing bottom (ADR 0020 Amendment 6). Long: check the board house's panel and price before M4. FOUR LAYERS, signal / ground / power / signal (ADR 0017 amendment 2026-09-29): layer 2 the PWR_GND plane with the analog island, power-entry-instrument.md section 2. WHITE SOLDER MASK, both faces (owner, ADR 0028): the top face is the LED row's first reflector. ASSEMBLY: JLCPCB assembles the parts whose sheet field Assembly is machine (the SMT passives, ICs, the LED row and the two surface-mount headers, J-MIDI and HDR-SERVICE). HAND-SOLDERED, Assembly=hand on the sheets: the thumb switches (SW1-n), the through-hole headers J-CHAIN x2, J-UMB and J-MCU, the U-BUCK module (THT SIP) and the breath sensor U-BREATH. The Matrix (U-MCU-RT) is on its own carrier board (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER), not this one: CBL-MCU-RIBBON reaches it from J-MCU. OPEN UNTIL tools/kicad.py check passes on hardware/boards/main-board and its fab/ is re-exported from the passing board

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, vertical, through-hole, keyed
description: The Matrix's connector on the main board: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from the Matrix carrier's J-MCU-C plugs in here, and unplugs with the lid raised
notes: PART: a 24-position 1.27mm shrouded, keyed box header standing straight up, through-hole, inside config/body.yaml boards.mcu_conn_* (the largest of the three below in each direction). BUY Samtec SHF-112-01-L-D-TH or Wurth 62702421621 (pre-fab review F3, 2026-11-22: the ribbon is Samtec's FFSD, which SHF is the mate for). The sheet carries XKB X1270WV-2x12A-9TV01, LCSC C5147231, 1A per contact [ds connectors/XKB-X1270WV-2xXXA-6TV01-1.27MM-BOX-HEADER-VERTICAL.pdf: the series drawing; its table has no 24 row, so the length is its formula, calc]. EQUALS: Samtec SHF-112-01-L-D-TH [ds connectors/SAMTEC-SHF-ESHF-EHF-ECF-CATALOG-PAGE.pdf; tail length and mouth not dimensioned there - measure before fitting], Wurth 62702421621 [drawing not banked: datasheets/MANIFEST.csv BLOCKED row; not cleared until it is]. STOCK IS THIN, 2026-11-21: XKB none at LCSC, Samtec none at DigiKey on a 6-week lead, Wurth 9 at DigiKey [web] - ORDER SPARES WITH THE FIRST BUILD (owner, 2026-11-21: 24-way, thin stock, carrier untouched; ADR 0018). The common 26-way header is not an equal: its thirteenth pad column lands in the Matrix carrier's fan-out. Footprint woody:IDC-Header_2x12_P1.27mm_Vertical (hardware/lib/README.md). Mates CBL-MCU-RIBBON's sockets - Samtec's SHF is that cable's own mate; another maker's header is a standard 1.27mm IDC fit to confirm on the first pair. WHERE: config/body.yaml boards.mcu_conn_at, its rows along the body, beside J-MCU-C (which hangs from the Matrix carrier's arm nearer the near edge), mouth up (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'J-MCU'). No part of the main board stands inside its keep-outs there ('Matrix ribbon', 'Matrix ribbon fold'). PINOUT: hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is the pin map (ADR 0018), ribbon conductor n = pin n, odd and even across the two rows, the odd row nearer the near edge, pin 1 at the mouth end. Every fast line has a ground, a supply or a static line on both sides but one: the LED data (IO1) lies between the ADC's MOSI and MISO, so the firmware sends no LED update during an ADC transaction (carrier.md, The pin map). Pin 6, the spare, is on ground. KEYED AND SHROUDED: a reversed plug puts 5V on a GPIO. RATING: the 5V and GND contacts carry the whole Matrix draw, and fed from the 5V pad nothing on the Matrix limits it (its USB diode is bypassed - matrix-led-current, power_path), so rate them against U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0), not against matrix-led-current: three 5V contacts at ~0.33A and five GND at ~0.2A each [calc, equal sharing], against the header's 1A per contact [ds XKB drawing above] and the cable assembly's rating (CBL-MCU-RIBBON).

part: 24-way 1.27mm IDC ribbon cable assembly, a 2x12 socket at each end, 2.50 in
description: The Matrix's wiring: J-MCU-C on the Matrix carrier to J-MCU on the main board
notes: PART: Samtec FFSD-12-D-02.50-01-N, a bought, tested assembly: 2x12 sockets both ends on the same face of the cable, polarised, pin 1 to pin 1 [ds connectors/SAMTEC-FFSD-1.27MM-IDC-CABLE.pdf; connectors/SAMTEC-FFSD-XX-X-XX.XX-01-PRINT.pdf]. FALLBACK IF 2.50 in IS NOT STOCKED: FFSD-12-D-02.00-01-N, which reaches with the lid raised but with only a few mm to spare (owner, 2026-11-22: 2.50 in, 2.00 in the fallback). Nothing longer: 3.00 in does not fold away under the lid. Stock of the 2.50 in length was not confirmed on that day [web]. CONDUCTORS: 24, conductor n = J-MCU pin n = J-MCU-C pin n (hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative, the Matrix carrier's sheet is held to it by tools/kicad.py check). EITHER END GOES IN EITHER HEADER: the two sockets are the same and each header's key takes it one way only. Folded once into the body, one socket faces down onto J-MCU, its key toward the near edge, and the other up into J-MCU-C, its key toward the far side. DO NOT FIT A CABLE WITH A REVERSED END (Samtec's -R option, or a hand-made one crimped end for end): it swaps every line and puts 5V on a GPIO. MATES J-MCU and J-MCU-C (J-MCU's row names the header): Samtec's own SHF is the pair this cable is made for; confirm the fit on the first pair if another maker's header is fitted. CURRENT: at U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0) the three 5V conductors carry ~0.33A each and the five GND ~0.2A [calc, equal sharing], inside the assembly's rating [ds, the cable page above]. RESISTANCE IS WHAT THE GROUNDS ARE FOR: ~34mohm per 100mm a conductor [from memory, ~30AWG]. The Matrix's 3V3 is the ADC's reference (carrier/breath-adc) and is regulated against the Matrix's ground, so LED return current in these grounds moves it. E11 confirms it: breath output clean while the matrix is exercised. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon length' is what the body needs between the sockets, the lid (which the carrier hangs from) held routing.chain_raise up, as the key chain's; the bought length is the next stocked one above it. Closed it lies in one fold toward the far side, over the main board and across the LED row between two LEDs ('Matrix ribbon closed: its legs and fold over the main board', 'Matrix ribbon crosses the LED row over no LED'). A DEAD MATRIX: lift the lid, unplug J-MCU, unscrew the carrier from the oak (three MECH-MX-SCREW), and replace the carrier with the Matrix on it, or desolder the Matrix's headers - nothing on the main board or the key boards is touched

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, vertical, through-hole, keyed - the same part as J-MCU
manufacturer: XKB Connection, Samtec or Wurth (J-MCU notes)
description: The Matrix ribbon's carrier end: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from J-MCU plugs in here, on the Matrix carrier's underside
notes: PART: as J-MCU (that row says which, and the sheet's fields carry it). WHERE: hung mouth down from the underside of the Matrix carrier's arm, its rows along the body, beside J-MCU on its near-edge side (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'matrix' 'J-MCU-C'; drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon's headers: side by side, not mouth to mouth'); its tails come out of the arm's top face. PINOUT: pin k carries J-MCU pin k; hardware/boards/matrix-carrier/matrix-carrier.kicad_sch is held to hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml by tools/kicad.py check. KEY TOWARD THE FAR SIDE, facing J-MCU, as the board's silkscreen says: the header is fitted half a turn from J-MCU's own way round, which is what lets a pin-1-to-pin-1 ribbon join them. A header fitted the other way round swaps every line. Assembly: hand

part: 1x10 2.54mm pin header, straight, surface mount, staggered feet, gold (hanxia HX PZ2.54-1x10P TP-YQ)
description: The Matrix's two pad rows to the Matrix carrier: a header standing on the carrier, through the Matrix's pads
notes: ONE PER PAD ROW, pin 1 at the Matrix's USB-C edge: the 5V..IO1 row and the IO33..RX row [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png]; the carrier's sheet names each pin for its pad. PART: hanxia HX PZ2.54-1x10P TP-YQ, LCSC C41417367: THE TOP OF ITS PLASTIC STANDS 3.2 +/- 0.2 ABOVE THE BOARD (config/body.yaml boards.matrix_hdr_h, which the Matrix sits on and which clears its back-side parts - drc.echo 'Matrix's back-side parts clear the carrier'): the insulator, 2.5 tall, stands on its surface-mount feet, and the drawing's end view dimensions the seating plane to the insulator's top; posts 6.0 above the plastic, staggered feet 5.0 across, gold [ds connectors/HANXIA-HX-PZ2.54-1x10P-TP-YQ.pdf]; JLC 1,090 in stock 2026-10-03. SURFACE MOUNT, NOT THROUGH-HOLE: J-MCU-C hangs under the carrier straight below the 5V..IO1 row's first pins, and a through-hole tail there would stand in its insulator. Type A (YQ) only; the footprint is that type's. BUILD: both headers soldered to the carrier's top face (by hand or JLC's assembly), the Matrix down onto their posts and seated on the plastic, its top face flat; solder both ends, then CUT THE POSTS FLUSH ON THE MATRIX'S TOP FACE and keep the joints flat - its top rises into the oak's relief (openings.matrix_relief_d). IO4 and IO5 reach nothing and are soldered for strength; IO6 is the MIDI output (midi-out.md). Assembly: hand
